The input-emission tail is measured from helper recognition using native event timestamps; app delivery is measured separately. This is not a hardware-to-OS interrupt measurement.
The first physical modifier paused input before the complete kill chord. A zero tail means no recorded synthetic event followed recognition; it is not an exact zero-time cancellation measurement.

The backend case SIGSTOPs an actual ComputerAutomationBrokerRuntime/DesktopComputerHost worker on the private production IPC channel. OS process state is checked before and after the chord; it resumes only for cleanup. The worker has no model or provider credentials.
The supervisor-stall attempts did not place both physical recognition and the complete chord inside the calibrated stall window. They remain failed and do not prove that case.
These are temporary synthetic AppKit apps with scripted per-app/session-action consent, a production controller and helper, and no Electron renderer or real overlay windows.
Signed installed-build/TCC attribution, complete real-app and multi-profile/display matrix, Windows desktop execution and full Electron failure testing remain pending.
Reports retain counts, booleans and relative timings, never key contents, typed values, screenshots, raw key traces or absolute uptime timestamps. Every release gate stays closed.
